title: Drop of Blood Emoji 🩸 Meaning: Donation, Periods, Injury
description: The drop of blood emoji 🩸 means blood donation, periods, injuries and medical tests, and it also shows up in horror and gaming. See each meaning and when to use it.
summary: 🩸 is a single red drop of blood. It is used for donating blood, for periods and menstrual health, for cuts, injuries and blood tests, and for gore in horror, Halloween and gaming. Unlike the other medical emojis, it was designed with periods in mind as one of its purposes.
meaning: Health and medicine are the plainest uses. Blood drives, donor appeals and hospitals use 🩸 to ask people to give, and donors post it after an appointment, often with a bandage. Patients reach for it when describing a blood test, a nosebleed or a paper cut. In these messages it is matter-of-fact, a visual label rather than an emotion.

Menstruation is the other major meaning. Before this emoji arrived, people talked about periods with stand-ins like a red circle, a tomato or a strawberry. The drop of blood was promoted in part by Plan International UK as a way to make periods easier to discuss openly, and many people now use it in that sense, including in period-tracking apps, health education and plain statements like “day one 🩸.”

Pop culture supplies a third set of meanings. Horror fans, true crime accounts, vampire stories, Halloween costumes and fighting games use 🩸 for gore, danger and drama. Gamers post it for damage, a bleed effect or a brutal match. In these settings it is theatrical, and a string of drops can be playful rather than alarming.

Figuratively, it stands for hard effort, as in “blood, sweat and tears,” and for family ties, as in being bound by blood or blood being thicker than water. These uses are less common but show up in captions about grueling training, long projects that finally shipped and close kin. Here the drop is a metaphor, and nobody is actually bleeding.

contexts.label: In health and donation
contexts.body: Blood services, clinics and volunteer groups use 🩸 to promote drives and thank donors. People share it after giving blood or plasma, sometimes with their blood type. It also appears in posts about anemia, blood sugar checks and lab results. The tone is informational, so pairing it with 🩹 or 💉 clarifies the medical sense.

contexts.label: For periods
contexts.body: People use 🩸 to say their period has started, to explain cramps or to cancel plans when they feel unwell. It is direct without being graphic. Health educators and campaigners use it to normalize the topic. Between close friends, a single drop can say everything; with others, a few words help.

contexts.label: In horror and gaming
contexts.body: Horror film fans, Halloween posts and dark fantasy accounts use 🩸 for blood and menace. Gamers post it for bleed damage, a gory finisher or a tough boss fight. It is common in bios and usernames for a dark aesthetic. In these settings drops are decorative and rarely meant literally.

examples.meaning: Sharing that the sender donated blood and naming a blood type.

examples.text: Can’t make it tonight, day one 🩸 and cramps
examples.meaning: The sender has just started her period and does not feel well enough to go out.
A minor kitchen injury that needed a bandage.
Planning to watch horror films, with blood as part of the theme.

examples.text: That raid boss had us bleeding out 🩸
examples.meaning: A difficult video game fight that caused heavy damage.

combos.meaning: A small cut or injury, now bandaged.
A blood test, a blood draw or donating blood.
Period pain or a rough first day of menstruation.
Horror and Halloween themes: slashers, gore and costumes.

confusedWith.difference: 💧 is a blue drop of water, used for water, tears, sweat and hydration. 🩸 is red and specifically means blood.
💉 is a syringe for vaccines, injections and blood draws. It focuses on the needle and medical procedure, while 🩸 shows the blood itself.
🫀 is a realistic heart organ, used for health, cardiology and intense emotion. 🩸 focuses on blood, not the organ, and is broader in use.

avoid: Do not use it carelessly around news of real violence, accidents or self-harm, where it can seem flippant.
Avoid it in work messages about absence unless you are comfortable signaling a period or injury to colleagues.
Do not send graphic combinations to someone who is squeamish about blood or medical topics.
design: A single teardrop shape in deep red, often with a highlight to make it look glossy. It matches the outline of the water droplet emoji but in a clearly blood-red color. Designs are consistent across major platforms, differing mostly in shade and shine.

faqs.a: Yes, it is commonly used that way. The drop of blood was promoted partly as a period emoji to make menstruation easier to talk about, and it is now widely used to say a period has started. It also has other meanings, such as blood donation and injury.

faqs.q: What does 🩸 mean in a text from a girl?
faqs.a: Often it means her period has started or that she has cramps, especially if she is canceling plans or saying she feels unwell. In other contexts it could mean a cut, a blood test or a horror movie. The words around it usually make the meaning clear.

It typically means damage, bleeding effects or a brutal fight. Players use it after hard boss battles, close matches or gory moments. It can also feature in clan names and usernames for a darker, aggressive style.

faqs.q: When was the drop of blood emoji added?
faqs.a: 🩸 became available in 2019 as part of emoji version 12.0. Before then, people had to use other red objects or the syringe as substitutes when talking about blood or periods.
